utterances.text: Since I was not a member of the Crisis Staff at the time, I think it was 10, up to 12, 13 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you know who initiated the establishment of the staff? I mean, how did it come about? Was it put on the agenda of something? I mean, it didn't, obviously for everyone in the courtroom, it didn't drop out of the air, so who initiated the establishment of the Crisis Staff, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have to know that in my position, but I believe that followed from some law or regulation that applied at the time in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... talking about persons, sir. What person initiated this action? Someone had to put it on agenda. Someone had to raise it. Again, it didn't drop out of the air.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dear sir, I repeat: At that time I was in a position at the time which did not require me to know who initiated this, and I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, sir, you've told us that you were not a member of the HDZ party, but you performed your function in the Crisis Staff and then when it became the War Presidency you performed your functions as a nominee of the HDZ, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you clarify the period, the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: From approximately the 11th of May, 1992, until you left that position, as you've told us, toward the end of October, early November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, on the 11th of May I was not a member of the Crisis Staff. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I really apologise. On the 11th of May, yes, I was. That was in fact the first day. On the 11th of May, I -- I was a member of the Crisis Staff of Jablanica. I thought it was the 13th when I began.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And during that time, your tenure, sir, you performed your functions as a nominee of the HDZ; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, before we go on on some of these other questions, let's -- I think it might be helpful to go back to some -- some basic items here. If I could ask -- I don't have all these because -- in hard copy in the courtroom, Your Honour, but if we could use e-court for those purposes for some of the maps, but for the record I'm referring to the Prosecution Exhibit P 09276, which the Chamber and others might recall is a book of maps that was distributed earlier in the case, and with the usher's assistance -- or the registry's assistance if we could show the witness map number 9 from book number 1 -- map book 1, which again is P 09276.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Map number 9, please. Page 10 in e-court, I believe. Sir, if you have that, and you can just look at it briefly. This is a map which the Chamber has previously admitted into evidence titled "Ethnic composition of Bosnia and Herzegovina, 1991." And if I can direct your attention in particular, please, to Jablanica and Konjic municipalities. You would agree with me, and I assume, sir, you have knowledge of this, that both Jablanica and Konjic were by a substantial measure Muslim majority municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you go to map number 25 in this same book, please, which I believe would be e-court page 26. There's a graph on the top of that page, sir, and would you agree with me that again I'm not even -- the percentage -- if I read the bar graph approximately, that in 1991 the Muslims represented approximately 80 per cent of the population of Jablanica municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the 1991 census, they accounted for 70 per cent of the population of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think to be exact, it was 72 per cent Muslim and 18 per cent Croat; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So not a majority Muslim just by a percentage or two, but in contrast 72 per cent Muslim versus 18 per cent Croat; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, when Mr. Karnavas asked you yesterday whether the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna or the HVO or any of these other entities that we talk about had ever carved any territory out of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you said no. And, sir, that's not really correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a mischaracterisation of the question. It had to do with Jablanica. We're speaking of Jablanica. The Prosecution's case is that throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina the Croatian Community is some sort of a map that you can draw around. We're trying to show that there are various communities. Here is just what -- one example. When we got to Gornji Vakuf, Uskoplje, we see something very similar. So if the gentleman wishes to pose questions, I would ask that they're based on the factual predicates which are in the record, that he not mischaracterise the record, that he not try to trick the witness, and that he be a little more respectful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no basis for any of that. I will find -- if I -- I'm going to need more time than four hours if I have to find any citation. This is not the way we've normally conducted business. I will be happy to find it. When I'm listening to direct examination, I take copious notes. I read them at night and I prepare my cross-examination, and I prepare them based exactly on what has been covered in court, and I have no doubt this matter was covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's not that difficult to find. It's at 33007 to 33008 where we find the precise question. So the issue between Mr. Karnavas and Mr. Scott I think can be resolved by specific reference to that. While I'm on my feet on this we had a reference few minutes ago, but just a practical thing. It's a hobby horse of mine, but since the transcripts are available now in the fully numbered version if an exercise is being done as it was a few minutes ago to find the reference it would be helpful to have that reference than page 14, and I believe it's just as easy to find the full numbered reference as it is to find the temporary one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, I'm grateful for Mr. Stewart for the citation reference. As to the practice of page numbers, Your Honour, Your Honours know we get a daily transcript. I have to prepare. I don't wait for the next day. I would like a little latitude at being able to conduct my cross-examination to the best of my ability, and you know, Mr. Karnavas is always saying how he stays up all night to do -- well, I do the same thing, and I do the best I can using the best available materials to me, and it may not be perfect, but I had a-appreciate the opportunity to conduct my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, let me put it to you that in fact Herceg-Bosna did claim territory on the territory of the sovereign State of Bosnia-Herzegovina, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please look -- direct your attention, sir, in the binder to P 0079. P 0079. It's not -- all right. Can we have it on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again, Your Honour, this directly flows from the necessity to continually adjust to cross-examination on a short basis documents that become relevant in the course of the questioning, and therefore cannot be put in a binder on the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you have P 0079. My apologies that it wasn't in the binder, but if you look on the screen, please. That is document that everyone in the courtroom, I think, is quite familiar with. The establishment of the so-called Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna on the 18th of November, 1991. Can I direct your attention, please, to Article number 2 where it says: "The territories of the following municipalities shall comprise the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna," and you will see a list of territories and in that list, I believe you'll see, sir, don't you, the municipalities of Konjic and Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It says areas, not territories, and I think there's a vast distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a list of municipalities in Article 2 which is stated as "shall comprise the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna"? You don't see that language, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if I can ask you, please, to go to the map book again which we looked at before, P 09276. Map number 3. Page 4 in e-court. Does that map not indicate, sir, by blue colouring and an exterior dark blue border the borders of the municipalities listed in Article 2 of Exhibit P 00079? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot count all these municipalities and compare them. That would take some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you see Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I see Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask the witness -- the question of the flags came up. Can I ask the witness to be shown it again for reasons cited previously, it may not be in the binder. If I can have the assistance of e-court -- perhaps it is in the binder. P 09520. P 09520.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: While we're on the map, Your Honour, perhaps he could ask the gentleman to carve out where exactly within the municipality of Jablanica or Konjic, if he knows, was the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. You're shaking your head, Judge Trechsel, but if you recall, there was copious questioning about this. To have a map that was designed by the Prosecution to show that because there is a statutory decision that says areas and now to put it into some kind of framework and then say, well, it's in there, isn't, therefore we've proved our point is not in my opinion evidence of which this Trial Chamber can or should rely on, rather, he can ask the gentleman to point out exactly where, in what part, there was within the Jablanica municipality a carved-out area, or whether it's the entire area, because that's the purpose of this cross-examination, and to show these documents is simply a waste of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I disagree, Your Honour, and counsel can conduct his re-examination if he so wishes. I will conduct my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you can look at P 09520. That is the flag of the Republic of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That is the flag of the Republic of Croatia; correct? P 09520. It should be on the screen. If anybody can't see it, I don't know why that's so difficult. Is that the flag of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the map of the republic of the Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Not the map the flag, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the flag of the Public of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can I nest ask you to look at P 09523. If it's easier to look at e-court, let's do that for the time being hopefully save a little bit of time. Sir, is P 09523 the flag or a flag of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a flag of the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in some instances is it fair to say, sir, that the map -- the two -- excuse me for saying that, the flags, that the flags are, in fact, often even more similar and that in some of the Herceg-Bosna flags, the shape of the shield, if you will, is the identical same shape as that of the Croatian flag? Sir, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again you're talking about Herceg-Bosna, sir. I told you this was the flag of the Croatian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's why I can't answer yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I see. Would you agree with me, sir, that that flag of the Croatian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina is often even more similar to the -- to the Republic of Croatia flag and that the shape of the shields, if you will, are identical in at least some versions of that flag?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe I bear a certain amount of physical likeness to another person that goes under a different name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, it appears from various prior statements that you've given that we can agree that in April 1992 a joint Muslim-Croat War Presidency was established in Jablanica and there is no question about the, if you will, the legality or the legitimacy of the crisis -- the Crisis Staff at that time which then became the War Presidency in Jablanica municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in terms of the relationship between the Croats and Muslims in Jablanica during this time period, I want to refer you to an earlier statement you made in 1996 and confirm, presumably, that you still believe that statement to be accurate. On the 13th of June, 1996, you gave a statement in which you said -- in which you divided the operations of the War Presidency into three different periods. First from its establishment, which in that statement was April 1992. I'm happy to amend that based on your testimony to May. But from its establishment to November 1992. This period is marked by the collaboration between the representatives of the Muslim and Croatian communities despite the fact that Serbs had been sidelined. Do you agree with that, that during that period, April to November 1992, the relationship between the Muslims and Croatian Community according to your statement in 1996 was that it was basically collaborative?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can agree with that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You said that the second period which you set from November 1992 until the appointment of Mr. Cibo around mid-March 1993, that during that period the Croats were no longer represented within the Presidency but the relations between the two communities remained good; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite. The Croats were in there for only two meetings of the War Presidency throughout that period and then they continued to take part until Cibo arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is, yes, that's correct. The Croat, you said, in 1996 the Croats were no loner represented. You've now said, okay, they attended two meetings but their relationships between the two communities remained good?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Correction. He said that they did not attend two meetings, but then they came back. That's what the gentleman indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's correct, thank you, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, sir, you said the third period which you began that period, if you will, with the appointment of Mr. Cibo and in this third period beginning with the appointment of Mr. Cibo and continuing, you said that was the period of conflict between the Muslims and Croats; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a conflict between the BH army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now the first president of the War Presidency was Mr. Sefer Hamdo until the 10th of June, 1992, and Mr. Hamdo was the -- excuse me -- followed by Mr. Nijaz Ivkovic. And forgive me if I haven't pronounced those correctly, but is that right? Those were the first two presidents of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Your pronunciation is good. And these were the first two presidents of the Crisis Staff or the War Presidency, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And it may be obvious for some in the courtroom, but for the purposes of the record, both of those men were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I take it there is no disagreement that -- or no issue that Mr. Ivkovic, for example, his -- his tenure -- his appointment and tenure as president of the War Presidency was completely proper and legitimate?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No disagreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And of course a significant majority of the Jablanica municipal government authorities was comprised of Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again going back to what we were looking at earlier the map, the demographic information that we discussed a few minutes ago, that's not really surprising, is it, given the fact that Jablanica municipality was 72 per cent Muslim; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, the outcome of the 1990 elections in Jablanica municipality were at least approximately the following: The SDA received 15 seats. The HDZ received 7 seats. The Serb party at the time -- at the time in 1991, obtained 6 seats, and then there was some other smaller parties, the reform party, received 2 seats et cetera. Is that generally consistent, sir, with your memory of the outcome of the 1990 elections for our purposes the primary focus being that the SDA won 15 and the HDZ approximately 7?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unable to agree with this. The Serb party did not get a single vote, the simple reason being back in 1990 at the Jablanica election, there was no Serb party involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Forgive me if I misspoke. It might have been my mistake. The SDA received 15 and the HDZ approximately 7; is that correct? Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that seems to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And some testimony came up, I don't know if it was the first or second day at this point, but it came up several times, and you were talking about an 80 per cent, 20 per cent split or apportionment, for example, on certain things concerning the division of goods or supplies or what have you, just a general example, for the ABiH would get 80 per cent and the HVO would get 20 per cent. Now, can we start with -- do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was something that was agreed in principle, but it was never something that was actually carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did that -- did that principle or this division arise or come at least in part out of the fact again of these two pieces of information we've talked about in the last few minutes, that is that the Muslims had 72 per cent of the population in the municipality and had won substantial majority of the seats in the 1990 elections and flowing from all that, an 80/20 split seemed about right. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't involved myself, and I don't know what exactly the people who made that proposal bore in mind at the time and what their principal ideas were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that that split roughly corresponds to the data we've looked at in the last few minutes?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The division of logistical support, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This 20 -- this 80 per cent, 20 per cent apportionment, sir, that you testified about in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was only in reference to logistical support for the armed forces, the HVO and the Muslim armed forces. That is the 80/20 split that you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas showed you a series of exhibits, and I'm not going to go to them all. I'm not going to take you through the content of them, but just for the record, and again so hopefully I can avoid being questioned about it. I refer to the record, for example, to 1D 01447, 1D 01448, 1D 00960. And I'll represent to you, sir, and I'm sure as we've already seen this morning, and I'm sure I'll be corrected if I'm wrong. These are documents that Mr. Karnavas showed to you that talked about efforts to I'll say retain resources and people in Jablanica. Stay here. Don't go elsewhere. We need people. We need the supplies to remain in Jablanica municipality. And this was all during the spring and summer of 1992. You generally recall that topic and those documents being shown to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, sir, wouldn't you agree with me that those were completely logical and prudent steps for the municipality to take during a time in which everybody agrees it was a time of crisis, hence the term Crisis Staff, to maintain and marshall and manage its resources to the best of its ability? Isn't that a completely wise decision?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the right decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, in connection with the HVO military aspects of these events, isn't it correct, sir, that throughout this period, from April, May 1992 until even the end of 1992, the Jablanica authorities, the ones we've been talking about this morning, were trying to bring -- repeatedly tried to bring the HVO military into a unified, unified defence system with other military forces, such as the new BiH Territorial Defence or TO which had been established in April of 1992, the Patriotic League. The repeated efforts by the Jablanica authorities to bring HVO been the same unified defence system; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct. What is correct is this: The HVO wanted to be treated as an equal defence component, and you talked about it being brought under something. It's not that it was being brought under something. All we wanted from the outset was for it to be treated as an equal defence component, same as the Green Berets, the Patriotic League, and the Territorial Defence. It wasn't a question of the HVO being brought under something, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Wasn't it the reality, sir, that the HVO was engaged in just exactly the opposite throughout this time period, and that was not only to not become part of the unified defence system but to assert HVO supremacy over all the other armed forces in the area, including Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I hear of it. Hear from you today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let's look at Exhibit P 00186 in the binder. My binder. Not that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could have the usher's assistance, please. He has the Petkovic binder there. That may cause confusion. If we could put the other one away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: P 00186. First document. Sir, that is decision by the Jablanica Municipal Council on the 6th of May, 1992, by the president, a man -- the man we mentioned -- one of the men we mentioned a few minutes ago saying, among other things, the decision is "in the territory of Jablanica municipality, a joint system of defence has been organised that shall include the Territorial Defence forces, the Croatian Defence Council, the Green Berets, and all others that will subordinate themselves to the single command of the Jablanica Territorial Defence." Now, as someone who was involved in Jablanica political matters and these affairs around this time, you certainly saw or were aware of this document, weren't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I was not involved in political matters as you suggest.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you repeat or rephrase your answer, sir, because the interpretation -- interpreters could not -- did not get it.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any political involvement because I think that's what you suggested firstly. Secondly, I was not a member of the Crisis Staff on the 6th of May, 1992. Therefore, I don't know what the Crisis Staff wanted to say when phrasing its decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, in the second paragraph it seems that there's going to be a public communique. Therefore, this decision is going to be made known to all the residents. You were one of the residents, weren't you, at the time? So you were not made aware of this as a simple citizen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. As an ordinary citizen. I wasn't a military man myself, but I was not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there was no communique, because here it is said that there's going to be one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all documents such as decisions or orders, not all of them were published, just those that were titled announcement, proclamation, declaration or something like that. These were broadcast over the local cable TV. But documents of this nature would not be published. As an ordinary citizen living in Jablanica at the time, I did not have occasion to read this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, maybe the translation is not correct. That happens sometimes. In the English text it has -- it says that citizens of Jablanica have been informed, have been informed. Not fall -- to be should, will eventually, have been informed. Maybe the text in Croatian says something different, but if it says the same thing your answer is really not convincing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I see that that's what it says, but that's not necessarily the case. It says here that everything was published, but that wasn't necessarily the case. Sometimes things weren't published that were expressly meant to be published. I'm not saying that this wasn't published. I'm saying I never saw it published. Anyway, we can't assume that I knew everything that was going on at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What Judge Trechsel had said about had been informed the Croatian says this decision actually takes effect as of now and the Jablanica population is to be informed by a public communique. So this is something that would follow, whereas in the English we see the perfect tense. It follows that we don't know whether it was, in fact, published or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, would you mind reading this second paragraph so that the interpreters can translate that. Please read it out, because there seems to be a problem in the translation. Please read out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 2, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "This decision takes effect immediately. The population of Jablanica shall be familiarised with this decision by a public announcement."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the French translation it's not quite the same. I believe the interpreter knows B/C/S, and it says: "And to make it public to the population, to make it known to the population by way of a communique." So in the French translation, it means that this text is to be made known. So it's not known yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It's even clearer in the English. It absolutely says "shall secure," and that is not at all what the translation says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, be that as all these wrinkles that we've talked about in the last few minutes, be that what they may or may not be, this is the 6th of May, 1992, and you've told us that at least by five days later, on the 11th of May, 1992, and then continuing on until at least the end of October 1992, you were a member of the War Presidency in one fashion or another. Are you telling the Chamber that you did not -- you were not aware of efforts by the Presidency during that time period to bring the HVO military within a joint system of defence as in concept outlined here?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Prosecutor, I have to repeat this. I don't like this term that you keep using, the HVO being brought under something. It simply is what it is. It is as it is, and it already is. It is a component, and it is a component of the joint system of defence or the joint armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, answer me this: How can it be a component of something the HVO declared to be illegal?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps he can point to where is it that in Jablanica the HVO declared something illegal like the Territorial Defence, because we're talking about Jablanica. That is very discrete area. I understand what the Prosecution is doing. I just didn't fall off the apple cart. I understand the technique, but this is the wrong person to use this technique with, because we -- the whole testimony was about what is happening in Jablanica, just like we're going to have somebody who's going to testify about Gornji Vakuf. So let's restrict the questioning to this area. What was happening elsewhere, we could do that with others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, my question stands. Counsel, I'll conduct my cross-examination. If it becomes -- if this witness tells the Chamber that he was sitting isolated in Jablanica and did not know what the HVO -- what was happening in the HVO structures, in the HDZ, in -- coming out of Mostar, if he tells the Chamber he doesn't know anything about any of that, then that's one thing, but that -- I don't think that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you will look, please, next to 5D -- it's the last document in the binder. 5D 04271. 5D 04271. Sir, this is an order by Mate Boban dated the 10th of April, 1992, converting all Crisis Staffs and municipal Territorial Defences -- staffs, et cetera, to the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council, and stating in paragraph 2 that these shall all be subordinated to the HVO Main Staff. Now, you knew that was the position of the HVO in the spring of 1992, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again I was no military man myself. I've never seen this before. I don't know anything about what you are asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So when you were sitting on the Presidency of the Jablanica municipality during the period May to end of October 1992, you're telling these Judges that the topic of the defence of Jablanica and the roles of the HVO and the roles of the ABiH and these other -- other -- potential other groups, that was not a topic of -- of conversation or meeting or discussion?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was often discussed at these meetings, regularly I might say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you please to next look at Exhibit P 00195, which should be the second document in the binder, sir, if that will assist you. P 00195. This is an order from the HVO Main Staff by someone named Ante Roso, declaring on the 8th of May, 1992, three days before you say you became a member of the Presidency that: Number 1: "The only legal military units in the territory of the HZ HB are units of the HVO." Number 2: "HVO Main Staff is their Supreme Command." Every member of the above military units must be HVO insignia ..." Item 4: "This order supersedes all orders of the Territorial Defence command which shall be considered illegal in this territory." Now, again did you not know what the position of Mate Boban and Mr. Roso and the HVO Main Staff and the HVO main government was during that time period?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no idea what the position was of Mate Boban or General Roso, and I can repeat for the hundredth time, I was not a military man in that period, and I didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for your information -- [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I'll speak Croatian. For your information, this document was refused for admission by your decision of the 17th of July. I think it was the signature that was in dispute. And this whole document should be considered with some reservations. I'm saying this now because I did not want to influence the answer of the witness. And we're wondering about the provenance of this document. It does not bear the normal stamp of the Croatian archives. We don't know where the Prosecution got it. And especially controversial is the signature, because it was added in handwriting. "General Ante Roso," everything is handwritten. It's not clear who signed this. And we dispute the whole signature and the document as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, regardless of this document, and thank you, Mr. Kovacic, for reminding us that this document had not been admitted, but apart from that, during the examination-in-chief, I understood that you did have some municipal duties. You were for a time president of the municipality. During that period a series of events took place, not only in Jablanica, also elsewhere. You might be right. You say, "Well, I wasn't aware of that." Fine. That's quite possible. However, when you have events that really affect Jablanica proper, it may seem surprising that you weren't aware of certain things. That's the source of our amazement. Also as an ordinary citizen because a citizen knows at least what happens -- what's happening. What do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can say this: The documents so far presented to me when I was asked to give a comment, some of them were written in Mostar. This particular one was written in Grude. But basically they are military documents. Even those written in Jablanica, if they are military in nature, I cannot know all about them. And especially those written in Grude and in Mostar. If they are strictly military documents, then I really don't know anything about them. And even if you present me with another hundred of this kind, I'll be only able to say I don't know anything. And, Your Honours, I was head of the local municipal government for a very definite period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't say that you were head, but that you had the title of -- of president, but when you are a president, you're not necessarily the chief. Best proof is that when you preside a Trial Chamber, you're not the chief of it. Please proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'd love to follow up that with questions, but in any event.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if -- let me direct your attention, and your answer just now, let me just point out to you is itself relevant to the Chamber, because in reference to the evidence you've given so far the fact that you say you now know very little about what happened in Jablanica on a military basis, the Chamber will certainly take that into consideration, but let me ask you about this: Do you recall that in July 1992 there were ongoing attempts to incorporate for the MUP, the M-U-P, the MUP as we call it, of Herceg-Bosna to take over and incorporate the Jablanica MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July 1992 there were no attempts whatsoever to incorporate the Jablanica MUP into the MUP of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you please go next to P 00321, which should be the fourth document in your binder, please. P 00321. Sir, this is a communication coming from the Jablanica municipality, Territorial Defence Staff, dated the 12th of July, 1992, addressed to Croatian Defence Council Jablanica, subject formation of joint Staff Command notification. And again talking about -- I'll put it to you again without reading the entire document, again a discussion of the unified defence system, and among things saying in point 2: "The newly formed Staff Command of the armed forces shall fight for a sovereign, single, civil and inseparable Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, shall respect and carry out only the orders issued by the Supreme Command and the Main Staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, despite whatever else you've said up until now, can you assist the Chamber at all with the reaction of the HVO in Jablanica to this communication? Either specifically or in general, sir. Something that was discussed at the time, was talked about in the community, because once again, sir, when you gave your testimony previously, you were quite -- quite more expansive than the information you provided to us.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm seeing this document for the first time, but I do know both as a member of the Crisis Staff and a member of the War Presidency that both the HVO and TO always informed these sessions that cooperation was good, but there were remaining logistical problems because the HVO sometimes got nothing, sometimes got less than what had been agreed. And as far as these military obligations were concerned, preparation, training, going out into the field, all that was very good. That's what I remember from the reports we got at the sessions of the War Presidency and the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, looking at the clock, this might be the time for the break I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was so fascinated by the document that I lost track of time. It's 12.30. Let's break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you can next turn in the binder to Exhibit 27 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Scott. I have still a question to the witness with regard to the last document we have looked at. That was P 00321. At that time, 12 July 1992, would you be so kind as to recall your function at that time? In Jablanica, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this time, on this date indicated here, I was the president of the Executive Board of Jablanica municipality, and ex officio I was member of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You were a member of the War Presidency, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And did you -- did you see to whom this letter was addressed by -- by Major Salihamidzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the name is Zijad Salihamidzic. I'm seeing this letter for the first time but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, it was addressed to the War Presidency, and I must say that it's a bit surprising that you as a member should not have seen it. A copy goes to the War Presidency. But you're sure you didn't look at that mail that came in in copies? You left that all to someone else, or how did this -- how did you do the job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me, I'll explain very briefly. The War Presidency operated in this way: The president of the War Presidency convened sessions, and all the background material, all the documents, including this one, when they arrived before the War Presidency, the president chairing the meeting would choose in what form, in what way he would inform the War Presidency. So in my particular case it should not be understood that the president of the War Presidency brought this paper and read it out to us. He certainly didn't, and he certainly didn't read it. And the War Presidency didn't work that way. If he had read it out to us, if I had attended the session, I would have had to remember this, but I don't remember that. I don't remember that he brought the paper and read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you can next go please to Exhibit P 00273. This is an order from Mate Boban, dated the 20th of June, 1992, addressed to Jablanica. 273. 00273. This is an order by Mate Boban. In the second paragraph he says: "I prohibit the HVO Jablanica Municipal Staff to issue any kind of certificates authorising exit or passage through the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna to people who reside permanently outside of the Jablanica municipality." Now, did this direction from Mr. Boban come to your attention any time during the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as military certificates are concerned, I had nothing to do with them, and I never saw them, but I heard something related precisely to the second paragraph of this letter. Namely, I heard it was prohibited to issue them to people outside the area of Jablanica municipality. In other words, people who simply happened to be in Jablanica municipality and wanted these certificates to be issued to them. I really don't know for what reason they were not eligible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The third paragraph references a man named Ivan Rogic. Who was Mr. Rogic, and what position did he have in -- on the 20th of June, 1992, in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time Mr. Ivan Rogic was the president of the HDZ in Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So you're saying that in this instance, it was the party president who could actually issue such documents; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I told you I had nothing to do with the certificates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Mr. Rogic is the man who succeeded you as -- when you left the council or the Presidency at the end of October 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us on what authority Mate Boban issued this order to the Jablanica municipal HVO staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You have no basis -- you have no knowledge of any basis for Mr. Boban to issue this. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's go to Exhibit P 00505. It should be the fifth document in your binder. P 00505. The B/C/S version will be behind it, sir. You'll see that. There's an English translation, and if you look behind, I believe you'll see the -- there you go. Sir, did you become familiar at any time with the Constitutional Court decision, and just so you know I'm proceeding chronologically in the documents I'm showing you, and now we've come to the 18th of September, 1992. Did you become aware during this -- around this time that the Constitutional Court had issued a decision declaring the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna illegal or unconstitutional?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you ever at any time here of this decision, or is this something you never knew anything about, never heard of before?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is another thing that I can honestly say I never heard of.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This was not something that was discussed by members of the Presidency when you were still a member of that body in the fall of 1992 after the 18th of September 1992? It wasn't a topic of discussion that the Constitutional Court had declared Herceg-Bosna illegal? It was never discussed?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely never was it discussed at the sessions in Jablanica municipality that I attended. We never discussed this decision of the Constitutional Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's interesting in line with one of the documents we looked at earlier today. If I can ask the witness please be provided again the Petkovic binder. I direct the courtroom's attention in the Petkovic binder that we had earlier today to Exhibit 4D 00454. Sir, this is a document that you looked at before, so you've already been asked questions about it. Interestingly enough, on the second page of the English version I -- I'll try to help you as much as I can with the other, with the B/C/S version. I think from what I can see it should also be on the second page of the Croatian version. In this meeting in which these actions of the BiH armed forces are discussed, interestingly enough it says: "Proceeding from the indicated as well as the resolution of the Constitutional Court of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the annulment of all regulations on the establishment of the so-called Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna," et cetera, which if you hadn't heard of it, apparently these people had. And let me ask you flowing from that the questions that were put to you on that document in terms of there being actions, plans to take over territories in Jablanica and Konjic. Sir, it's correct, is it not, that on the 20th of March, 1993, all of the territory of Jablanica municipality belonged to the internationally recognised State of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct? All of it.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And all of the territory of Konjic municipality belonged to the internationally recognised sovereign state of Bosnia and Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So in terms of the military having any plans to either retain or regain control over that territory, would you agree with me, sir, that it's the -- it's usually the practice of most states to seek to maintain and, if necessary, recover its state territory?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I'd like to object to this question. This question presupposes that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was an army that represented the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, meaning all its three constituent peoples. I believe that it has been proven in these proceedings that three constituent peoples existed and each of them had its own army. So I object to this question because of the implication it contains, and I suggest my learned friend Mr. Scott reformulates this -- his question by saying whether the army of one entity has the right to liberate "other areas belonging to other entities."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... the question, but you oppose it, you object because your argument is different, but the Prosecutor has another argument. So the Prosecution develops his argument, and you are developing this. You can't prevent the Prosecutor developing his arguments by an objection. Now, the Judges will see who is right, but for the moment let the Prosecution ask his question and the witness answer or doesn't answer, and eventually you may come back on this point when the time comes. At this stage I think this is premature to try and prohibit the Prosecutor to develop his argument. All he needs to do is sit down and wait until Defence will speak on its own and alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may, just for one second. I don't -- I take the Court's observations and ruling, and I don't know whether the last question from the Prosecution stems from this particular document. I do find, however, the manner in questioning to be improper. He was asked about when he was sitting as president -- when he was participating in the War Presidency or was in the Crisis Staff. We already know that period of time. He gave an answer. He was then shown a document that obviously he was not a participant during those meetings but also the date is 20 March 1993, and of course what is happening in this particular meeting that is -- on this particular date, you know, they may be discussing something, but I don't see how you can connect this document with his previous answer. And so in that -- in that way I do object to the manner of this sort of cross-examination. I'm hopeful that this is not being lost on the Trial Chamber, that, you know, you can't be showing a document much later, where he's not a participate, where it's being generated by other institutions and then use that as a basis for somehow linking it to whether he had prior knowledge. It's just -- it doesn't flow. And I would welcome the opportunity to debate the point with any member of the Trial Chamber if they feel that there is a need to take exception to what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, on the question of timing, certainly it shows a real problem. Either he took part in the meeting and then he can speak about it, in particular the meeting on the 28th of March, 1993, or he wasn't present. So to integrate your question, try and integrate it within the field of the question in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me respond in general before I proceed, and that is -- I mean, I think this further illustrates the dramatic differences we're seeing with this witness on cross-exam -- what's real cross-examination and direct examination, and this document, the very document that was put to the witness with this date, dated the 28th of March, put to him by the Petkovic defence and asked questions about it. So how can it be out of time for the Prosecution but not out of time for the Petkovic defence? Absolutely. But specific questions about this document and the interpretations of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The problem, Your Honour, is this: I'm not suggesting that he cannot use the document. That's not my point. My point is, the question is whether he -- whether this matter was discussed while he was a member of the War Presidency, during that period. So now we have to put it within that context, the period from A to Z, whatever that period might have been. Okay. Now this document falls outside the period and certainly he is not -- as far as I understand, he's not present at the meeting. So how can you use that document as the basis of trying to suggest that he would have known or that there were hearings or discussions about this matter much earlier? That's what I'm suggesting. There is no linkage. And to -- to use that as a form of impeachment is, you know, we're missing a few steps. Now, if he can link it up, if he can establish it, that's fine. If he wants to show that later on this was a discussion, that's fine too. I don't have a problem. But to say that there was a meeting later on, and based on this meeting we know or should know that probably there was a meeting earlier, that you would have attended and therefore you're confabulating, I think it's a bit of a stretch. And my point was merely to point this out to the Trial Chamber because I certainly don't want the Trial Chamber later on to say, well, obviously he's confabulating. And as I indicated, I'm sure that this wasn't lost on the Trial Chamber's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, I think I understand. The first problem is, did the witness take part in this meeting. If he did take part in it, maybe he can answer your question on the content of this meeting. If he did not take part in the meeting, then it becomes more difficult. But even if he didn't take part in the meeting he may know something about the documents. I don't know where you intended to go to from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I refer to today's transcript at page 30, starting at line 19 when Ms. Alaburic said: "All right now 4D 454, a document prepared for you by the Prlic Defence. I won't be pursuing this document with you in great detail, with great respect to my good friend, then she proceeded to do that, but this is a report from a meeting of certain units of the BH army and rather their commanders, the Ministry of the Interior, et cetera, the date being the 28th of March, 1993. Sir, Witness, have you ever seen this document before? Answer, yes, but I believe that was 10 years ago at the very least. Next question: All right. I'll be asking you no more than three things by way of clarification. Paragraph 4 of that document is a decision of sorts to establish full control of the free territory using army and MUP forces. In your understanding of this document, this term full control of the free territory, does it mean that the army and the MUP intended to completely eliminate the HVO from that territory? I mean, that is -- so I don't understand, Your Honour. I don't understand. The Defence can ask about the document and the interpretation of it, and the Prosecution can't talk about the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Maybe the error's on my part. And I will confess error if that is the case. Confession is always good for the soul. Now, it was my understanding that the document was being used for the previous question that he was trying to elicit, and that is the decision on the unconstitutionality of the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. That was my understanding of it. Now, if he wants to use it for some other purposes, that's fine, but that was my point. Because the way the questioning went, and I'm -- you know, I'm a trained listener. It would appear that once he didn't get the answer that he wanted, or he set up the trap, as it were, then he went to the document to impeach. And the problem with the impeachment process is we have different dates different meetings, and there's no indication, no factual basis, no predicate that this gentleman would have known at the time, so maybe -- and I'm if I'm wrong, I stand to be directed but I'm not suggesting that the Prosecution -- let me be clear -- I'm not suggesting that they cannot use the document, but not for the purposes of impeaching the witness as to whether at the time he was a member of the Presidency of the Crisis Staff that there was a discussion concerning the decision that was reached by the Constitutional Court in Sarajevo at that time. That's the basis of my objection. And I hope I made it clear. I apologise to my learned friend if I misunderstood his methods or motives. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Especially with the witness about setting traps and that sort of discussion. I don't think is appropriate, but I do but I do appreciate Mr. Karnavas at least explaining where he was coming from because, with great respect, he is in error. That was not the purpose of showing him this document. The purpose in showing the document was twofold. It did -- there was a transition from the earlier question about the decision the Constitutional Court to this, and I just -- in making that transition, when this is a witness who does say, No, we never talked about it, and I just thought for the Chamber's general -- I guess it's impeachment of a more general sort. He says, isn't it interesting that these people certainly seem to be very well aware of it and were citing it as a basis for their programme. We have this decision. We've got to do this. That's all. It stopped there. Then it was put to the -- then that document was put to the witness by Ms. Alaburic for the -- and I submit for the purpose of showing something sinister. There was a plan by the ABiH to regain this territory, and Your Honour, my point, and I'll say it in front of the witness, is quite transparent. Yeah, to regain its own sovereign territory, its legal territory. That's the point, and it has -- so it was used with the witness by the Defence to make that point. I'm coming back and responding to exactly that evidence with the same document, so I'm at a loss as to know how there's anything improper about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't want my reaction to go unrecorded. My objection was about the presumption contained in the question. Its legal territory of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina with was the army of one of the three constituent peoples in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, everybody has said his bit or her bit so now put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I hope all that time will not be counted against me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, my question on this point in fact if we could go back pages in the transcript. The specific concept was put to you simply was this and it was a very basic one, and I just said, Is it anything unusual that a state -- leave out the armed forces -- a state would take actions to protect, retain, or if necessary, recover its sovereign territory? Does that strike you as anything unusual or odd about that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Much esteemed Prosecutor, you have to know that this decision of the Constitutional Court was not even common knowledge in Jablanica. No one knew about it. In a purely physical sense we were not receiving any newspapers from Sarajevo at the time. I simply cannot believe that there was actually an Official Gazette that reached Jablanica containing that decision and --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. Is there anything unusual about a state taking action to defend, protect, or recover its sovereign territory? That's my question now.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Mr. Prosecutor, what I find highly unusual is that you are so adamant that I should say something that I'm simply unable to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, we'll leave that. That's for the Judges to determine, sir. Now, is it correct that the Herceg Stjepan brigade, the HVO brigade, was formed in the Konjic-Jablanica area around late September 1992, or is that something else you don't know?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that, but I think it was set up sometime earlier on in 1992. This strikes me as late. I think it was set up somewhat earlier in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall the War Presidency, the body of which you were a member, on the 25th of September, 1992, asking the HVO to jointly produce a defence plan for the municipality and the HVO refusing to participate in that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I remember is the HVO making a request. I think that's actually on the record, and one of the documents that we talked about in chief there was the record where you saw the president of the HVO at a meeting of the War Presidency being adamant that a joint defence plan should be drafted for Jablanica municipality to keep such incidents from happening as the HVO forces heading one way and the Muslim forces the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now perhaps you can answer my question. You recall the War Presidency itself asking the HVO to participate in the preparation of a joint defence plan and the HVO refusing?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO made an independent request to be treated as an equal component in the defence of Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you please go next to Exhibit P 00539. It should be the sixth document in the binder. P 00539. While you're looking for it, sir, this is an HVO military police document dated the 1st of October, 1992, a report. Under item number 1, for example, it talks about the military police Jablanica executed the protection of the premises where the civil and wartime headquarters of the HVO Jablanica are located. Item 5 talks about the operation of a check-point at Risovac. Were you aware around this time in October 1992 that the HVO military police was operating in Jablanica municipality and operating a check-point at a place called Risovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that the HVO had a check-point at Risovac, Jablanica municipality. I do, however, also remember that the check-point was not being manned by military policemen alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, can you next go, and I'm going to need the assistance of the registry on this because again this was a document that came up -- became relevant after we prepared our binders?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just while we're doing that, two points. On the previous question there was an attempt to impeach. Now, the gentleman has an obligation to put his case to the witness. The gentleman indicated that he -- that he recalled the HVO making the proposal. The Prosecution insisted that it was the other way around with the War Presidency thus leaving us with -- under the impression that there was some sorts of minutes of the meeting that would contradict the witness. I suggest that if he is not going to put his case to the witness through some sort of a document, then it's my understanding that he has accepted the gentleman's answer on that. Otherwise, I am going to say that this is some sort of a trap. Secondly with respect to this last issue that was raised, I dare say we need to look at item number 5 where it talks about the reserve troops of the MUP, the Ministry of Interior. I highlight again -- it's under -- it's under 4. It's under -- I have it under number 5 here, check-points. Under check-points protection. So we see the MUP as consistently what he has indicated in his direct examination were involved, the [indiscernible] of troops. So I don't want to disrupt the Prosecution in any shape or form, however, I do think we need to be fair with the witness. If he's going to try to impeach him, then he needs to either show him the entire portion and put it into context, but more importantly, put his case through it. He can't just simply suggest through the question and then move on without trying to show that the gentleman's answer is anything other than truthful and complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if we can go next please to Exhibit P 0 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Scott, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, if the witness fails to answer a question, the Prosecutor has inevitably to try and get -- elicit an answer from him. This is the reason why he uses appropriate documents. Please continue, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you could turn next and again as I started to say, I think it's already on the screen -- no? Isn't it? I'm looking for Exhibit P 00546. And what I started to say a moment ago is that this is a document that became relevant after we prepared our binders, so if we can work in e-court, I'll appreciate it. But it was shown by the witness -- it was shown by Mr. Karnavas to the witness. I don't have his binders with me at this point. If the Chamber does, it's in the Prlic Defence binder, but it's Exhibit P 00546. Sir, it's also on the screen in front of you, and, sir, this was shown to you the other day. It is a -- it's minutes of the Presidency of the Jablanica municipality on the 6th of October, 1992. You are indicated as being present at this meeting as a member of the Presidency, and I'd like to direct your attention, please, to, in particular, to page -- it's the same passage that Mr. Karnavas showed to you. It starts on the bottom of page 7 of the English version. I'm afraid I'm not sure I can help you with the B/C/S version, sir, but it's the same paragraph that Mr. Karnavas showed you starting with the words Salko Zerem informed. It should be well back into the document. It comes after an intervention by Matan Zaric. If anyone in the courtroom could be kind enough in the B/C/S version to help us, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Page 5. Page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Page 5 of the Croatian version, sir, if you have that. You were read a lengthy passage in respect to something Mr. Zerem said, but let me read you the next sentence and then put a question to you. I will start about halfway through that paragraph on the bottom of page 7 of the English version. I'm just picking up for part of what Mr. Karnavas read: "It is necessary to say that the Muslims were neither organised nor ready at the beginning to fight against the aggressor and for that reason, they are also very grateful to the Croatian nation for their timely engagement and brave fight against the aggressor." Here's the part that was not read: "National units were rejected as unacceptable from -- as an unacceptable form in the structure of the RBiH and there is a greater chance of forming territorial units." Do you remember that discussion and that statement being made by Mr. Zerem?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you should see Mr. Zerem's statement in the overall context of discussions going on at the time. Mr. Matan Zaric at page 2 of this document in the B/C/S version, which is what you call it, is also on the record as saying the problem was there was no coordinated defence plan, agreed defence plan. That's at the beginning of that huge paragraph in the second part and that was what was leading to all this misunderstanding. I was present at the meeting at the time, and it was no problem at all. Zerem and everybody else at that meeting, they were saying that they were expecting the authorities to back both of the components alike in terms of logistics, the Croat component and the Muslim component. My impression at the time was that you wanted me to say something about merely one of the halves of this sentence uttered by Mr. Zerem, but I don't think there were any problems there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Wasn't that the consistent position of the Muslim members of the Presidency and the Muslim authorities or portion of the authorities in Jablanica municipality during this time? They were continually responding and saying to the HDZ and the HVO we reject -- essentially we reject Herceg-Bosna, we reject entities based on nationality. We reject all this, and we will not be part of it. Isn't that the communication that they continually sent which, I mean, let's jump to the chase, ultimately leading to the conflict because they wouldn't do what the HVO wanted them to do; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what they kept saying, and I wasn't under the impression at all while attending these meetings that what you are suggesting was actually taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's go, please, to the next exhibit which should be in the binder. Ninth document in the binder, P 00624. P 00624. A number -- another meeting just a few weeks later on the 22nd of October, 1992. And I will take -- remind the Chamber of what happened in Prozor a day or two after that date. And, sir, this is another minutes, set of minutes where you attended the meeting. You're listed in the "Others present" portion, Mirko Zelenika. And if I can, please, refer you to -- and I'll refer first the courtroom, the English speakers to page 6, the bottom of page 6 of the English version, and again, sir, I think you were directed at this before, but it's the paragraph that starts "If we wish to create a better environment for a more successful defence of the municipality more contacts and cooperation between the OS and the HVO are needed, there should be barracks with trained soldiers in Jablanica, and we need more support from the Municipal Assembly in general."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Page 5 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Page 5 for the witness, I thought. Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. I thought looking over his shoulder, so to speak, that he had it but thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Continuing on: "It should be openly said that the Muslim people will not accept three ethnic entities which are currently being imposed, and any attempt to implement it at all cost would provoke a civil war." Now once again, sir, I ask you again, wasn't that the consistent position and message coming from the Muslims at this time that any attempt to create ethnic entities, any attempt to do so would be rejected and would indeed lead to war?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, are we talking about the 22nd of October meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir. P 00624.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where you got this from. I never said a single word about the army. On the 22nd of October, this is the last page of each of the versions you will see me talking about the difficulties encountered in this work about the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you please answer my question. [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer your question because you're asking me something I didn't say. I never said a single word about the army at any of these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I said -- forgive me. If I misspoke, my apologies. If I misspoke or was mistranslated or something, my apologies. Mr. Karnavas had shown you starting at the bottom of page 6 of a passage, if we wish to create. We looked at that. No one attributed it to you, at least I didn't. And then it goes on to say: "It should openly -- it should be openly said that the Muslim people will not accept three ethnic entities which are currently being imposed and any attempt to implement it at all cost would provoke a civil war." And my question to you, sir, was following up the question -- the theme of questions that I've been putting to you for the last few minutes, was that, again, not a further statement of the consistent position and message coming from the Muslim side in Jablanica during this period rejecting any form of national entities, separate groups, separate military forces and proposing over and over again a single, for example, unified defence? I'm not asking whether you agree with it or not. Wasn't that their position as stated over and over again?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember now this is what Mr. Salko Zerem said. He led this debate not based on the situation and the relations in Jablanica municipality, rather, he was talking about something further away in Central Bosnia, something not in our own environment. This particular debate and what you see reflected here was not about the relations or indeed the situation in Jablanica itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, sir, following this, because our time is limited, even around -- and this is dated in October -- at the end of October 1992, wasn't it the case even through this period that the Muslim members of these authorities continued to reach out and include Croats in these -- in these matters, including when you -- you yourself, in fact, you told us much earlier now but referring back, you replaced a Muslim. You a Croat came on the Presidency replacing a Muslim. Mr. Matan Zaric, a Croat, was vice-president of the War Presidency. When you left you were replaced by a Croat, Ivan Rogic. So despite these building tensions, if you will, every effort was still being made to include Muslim -- or excuse me, Croats in these authorities; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct at all. What do you mean including Croats? This is their right under the constitution and according to election results. This is self-implicit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then we looked at the documents, sir, yesterday, I believe it was yesterday, 1D 03038. We may not need to look at that, but that is the document which you indicated was the one that relieved you of your position as a member of the Presidency or president of the Executive Council and then appointed you to a position in the public security station in Jablanica. Do you recall the document generally?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I'm still not quite sure about where you came out in terms of your involvement at the public security station. Are you saying you never actually performed that work? You never became part of that organisation? You never received payment or salary for any work in connection with that organisation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I agree with what you suggest. I went there several times. I didn't do anything, and I certainly received no salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You received no salary. Is that your -- all right.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I didn't do anything for them either. I received no salary, but there was nothing to receive a salary for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention next to Exhibit P 00832. It should be the tenth document in the binder. P 00832.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat that number for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: P 00832. Sir, this is a report from the minister of interior of MUP of the Bosnia -- of the Republic of Bosnia Herzegovina, dated 30 November 1992. In the second paragraph it says: "Since recently in some municipalities which have illegitimately declared themselves as constituent parts of the so-called Herceg-Bosna, one is organising police stations whereby members of the MUP of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina are being put under different sorts of pressure to sign application forms and requests for employment at the MUP of the so-called Herceg-Bosna. In that context one is issuing ultimatums to sign application forms and submit requests under the threat of termination of employment." Now, this is coming from Jablanica. Did you -- can you assist the Judges with to what extent the MUP of Herceg-Bosna was operating in Jablanica on -- around the end of November 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may make a slight correction, Your Honour. This is coming from Sarajevo, not from Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies. I accept that, Counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall the extent that the MUP of Herceg Bosna was operated in Jablanica around this time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Herceg-Bosna MUP was operating to no extent at all in Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, when you say "no extent," should we understand that the Herceg-Bosna, the MUP didn't exist in Jablanica municipality in November 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. So now it existed, but it wasn't doing anything?
